{{Quote|You're practically a corporation! Impressive... but where's the romance?|Han Solo, to Crimson Jack|<ref name="marvel12">[[Star Wars (1977) 12|''Star Wars'' (1977) 12]]</ref>}}
During the era of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the [[Pirate Master]] [[Crimson Jack/Legends|Crimson Jack]] led a '''gang''' that became notorious on the [[Hyperspace route/Legends|starlanes]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]]. Originally a group of bandits that robbed [[Spice/Legends|spice]] caravans on the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] frontier, the gang came into possession of a damaged [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] after the [[Battle of Toprawa]], which allowed the outfit to take its operation to new heights.

In [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], the gang captured and imprisoned notorious [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] and [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] hero [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], who promised to lead the gang to a lucrative Rebel treasury on [[Drexel/Legends|Drexel]]. However, Solo and his friends slipped away from the [[Crimson Jack's battlecruiser|battlecruiser]] once they reached the [[Drexel system/Legends|Drexel system]], leading to a heated [[Battle of Drexel|battle]]. During a [[Starfighter combat/Legends|dogfight]] between Jack's [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] and Solo's [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']], Jack abandoned his right-hand woman, [[Jolli]], after her [[BTL Y-wing starfighter/Legends|Y-wing]] was grievously damaged. Infuriated by his betrayal, Jolli flew her disintegrating craft on a suicide run into the [[Cruiser/Legends|cruiser's]] munitions deck, causing an explosion that annihilated Jack's operation. In the chaos, Solo shot and [[Death/Legends|killed]] Jack, bringing an end to him and his gang.

==Description==
{{Quote|I don't know who our over-eager host is, but one thing's certain: he sure gets around! X-wingers... TIE-fighters... every kind of small battle-spacer I've seen! And I've been from one end of the galaxy to the other!|Han Solo|<ref name="marvel7" />}}
[[File:Crimson_cruiser.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The gang's flagship, a refitted Imperial Star Destroyer.]]
During the era of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the charismatic, red-bearded [[Pirate Master]] known as [[Crimson Jack/Legends|Crimson Jack]] led a [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] gang that preyed upon and robbed [[Starship/Legends|starships]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="marvel7" /> Specifically, Jack's gang claimed an area in the Outer Rim that included the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Aduba-3/Legends|Aduba-3]] as their "sector."<ref name="marvel11">[[Star Wars (1977) 11|''Star Wars'' (1977) 11]]</ref> By [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], Jack's gang operated out of a massive former [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] he had chanced upon after a Galactic Civil War battle.<ref name="marvel7" /> The acquisition of the [[Crimson Jack's battlecruiser|battlecruiser]] necessitated a fundamental change in Jack's operation: he had to seek out funding from outside investors to afford the repairs to the damaged warship, promising a cut of future profits in exchange. While the gang had started by ambushing [[Spice/Legends|spice]] caravans on the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] frontier, it now had bona fide shareholders.<ref name="marvel12" />

Jack found the battlecruiser drifting in [[Realspace/Legends|space]], and often used a similar tactic when targeting upon passing ships: Jack would lure curious [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] in by making the [[Cruiser/Legends|cruiser]] appear to be a drifting, lifeless hulk, before launching his [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] and catching his prey unawares.<ref name="marvel7" /> However, Jack preferred not to chance full-out battle, instead using his fighters to usher the ship into his cruiser's [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beam]] and capture them whole before boarding and robbing them.<ref name="marvel7" /><ref name="marvel15" /> He also preferred to keep his targets alive, if possible, feeling that killing was an unnecessary waste of a potential revenue stream&mdash;<ref name="marvel7" />however, he was not above ordering his men to kill captives brutally if he felt it served a purpose.<ref name="marvel11" />

By 0 ABY, Jack's gang consisted of dozens of men, who although entirely [[Human/Legends|Human]], came from a widespread number of diverse backgrounds and who outfitted themselves with a variety of eclectic arms and armor. Crew members outfitted themselves with [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]], archaic [[cutlass]]es and other weapons, while at least one was known to wear full Imperial [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtrooper]] armor when boarding ships. The gang's starfighter arsenal was similarly varied, consisting of [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wings]],<ref name="marvel7" /> [[BTL Y-wing starfighter/Legends|Y-wings]],<ref name="marvel15" /> [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE fighters]] and several other different kinds of craft.<ref name="marvel7" />

==History==
===Meeting Han Solo===
{{Quote|Up to the bridge... and start computing our course to the Drexel system! Never thought I'd be saying this to a spice-smuggling sharpie like you, Solo... but you actually seem to have told the truth!|Crimson Jack, to Han Solo|<ref name="marvel11" />}}
[[File:CrimsonJackSolo.jpg|thumb|right|225px|Crimson Jack and Han Solo on the way to Drexel.]]
Crimson Jack's gang got its start ambushing [[Spice/Legends|spice]] caravans on the Outer Rim, crossing paths with outlaws and lowlifes such as the [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]].<ref name="marvel7" /> Originally operating out of a single [[DP20 gunship/Legends|DP20 frigate]], the gang stumbled upon a major upgrade during the Galactic Civil War. After a landmark Rebel victory over the Imperials<ref name="marvel12" /> in the [[Battle of Toprawa]],<ref name="gg">''[[Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope]]''</ref> the gang came across a drifting Imperial Star Destroyer that had been heavily damaged in the fighting. After dispatching a trio of TIE fighters, the gang boarded the cruiser, initially intending to merely scavenge what they could and move on. However, Jack noticed that most of the damage to the ship appeared to be superficial, and after eliminating the ship's few surviving defenders, decided to take the Star Destroyer as his new [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]]. The cost of repairing the cruiser was massive, but Jack managed to find several wealthy backers&mdash;<ref name="marvel12" />among them, notorious [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]]&mdash;<ref name="marvel37">[[Star Wars (1977) 37|''Star Wars'' (1977) 37]]</ref> willing to bankroll the repairs in exchange for a share of future profits.<ref name="marvel12" />

In 0 ABY, that included ambushing Solo, who by then had become a [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] hero for his actions in the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. Disguising his battlecruiser as an abandoned ship, Jack lured Solo's [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] in before launching his starfighters and chasing Solo into his tractor beam. Jack, [[Jolli]]&mdash;a relatively recent addition who had quickly become one of his most trusted guns&mdash;and a large boarding party thoroughly ransacked the ship, coming away with a large amount of treasure confiscated from Solo's smuggling compartments.<ref name="marvel7" /> Jack then let Solo go on his way, but not before leaving a [[Homing beacon/Legends|homing beacon]] behind on the ship. Soon afterward, Jack's gang found an even more interesting prize traveling alone on the starlanes: [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], a major Rebel leader.<ref name="marvel11" />

Although Jack believed that he could secure a hefty ransom from the Rebels for Organa, he was unable to get the stubborn Princess to give up the location of their base. However, the reappearance of Han Solo gave Crimson Jack an idea. With his tracer still aboard the ''Millennium Falcon'', Jack had always intended to swoop down on Solo again if he found him in his territory, and it was not long before he captured the ''Falcon'' again near the planet Aduba-3. This time, Solo allowed himself to be tractor beamed without a fight. Jack planned to use Solo and his [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] companion [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] to get Organa to budge: specifically, he meant to kill them slowly and brutally in front of the Princess, to show her give her an example of what would be in store for her if she didn't cooperate.<ref name="marvel11" />

However, the execution didn't go as planned. Jack's gang didn't account for the freakish fortitude of the Wookiee Chewbacca, who simply waded through the lower-power blaster bolts and incapacitated and disarmed several of Jack's men. A stalemate forced, Solo offered to parley with Jack, promising that he could help them acquire a much greater treasure than the one they had previously taken from his ''Millennium Falcon''. Intrigued, Jack accepted Solo's offer, meeting him for a feast in his quarters. There, Solo revealed that he and the Princess were previously acquainted: in fact, the treasure Jack had stolen from the ''Falcon'' was actually a reward from the Rebels for rescuing Organa from Imperial captivity. As such, Solo had gained knowledge of the supposed Rebel treasury in the [[Drexel system/Legends|Drexel system]], which he offered to lead Jack and the gang to in exchange for a cut of the proceeds. Although Solo had previously given Jack little reason to trust him, the promise of Rebel riches was too much for the pirate to ignore, and he ordered his ship full speed ahead to the Drexel system.<ref name="marvel11" />

===Chaos in the Drexel system===
{{Quote|Solo! I might've known it'd come down to just you and me&mdash;''"<br />"''No, Jack&mdash;just me!|Han Solo kills Crimson Jack|<ref name="marvel15" />}}
As [[Drexel/Legends|Drexel]] was far afield from Jack's gang's usual hunting grounds, their [[Navigation computer/Legends|navicomputer]] did not have much data on their destination. However, Solo had much more detailed charts on the ''Millennium Falcon'', and Jack allowed Chewbacca to tap into his battlecruiser's computer system to transfer their data.<ref name="marvel11" /> The connection finished as the battlecruiser arrived out of [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] at Drexel. There Jack found, to his fury, that Drexel was a [[Waterworld/Legends|waterworld]], meaning to him that the Rebel treasury could not possibly be on the planet.<ref name="marvel12" /> A heated confrontation on the ship's [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]] was interrupted, however, with a sudden [[Gravity/Legends|gravity]] disturbance that started to bring the cruiser lurching down towards Drexel's surface: the result of planetside [[Ship-dweller|ship-wreckers]] that used a [[sonic jammer]] to ensnare visiting vessels. In the frenzy and the confusion, Solo, Organa and Chewbacca managed to make it to the ''Millennium Falcon'' and flee to the planet's surface, taking out several crewmembers and ravaging the gang's starfighter arsenal on the way.<ref name="marvel13">[[Star Wars (1977) 13|''Star Wars'' (1977) 13]]</ref>

[[File:CrimsonJackDeath.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Crimson Jack meets his end at Han Solo's hands.]]
Although Jack was furious at Solo's escape, all his gang's energy had to be devoted to keeping the cruiser from being dragged to the planet below. With the ship's emergency drive maintaining a tenuous stalemate against the sonic jammer,<ref name="marvel14">[[Star Wars (1977) 14|''Star Wars'' (1977) 14]]</ref> Meanwhile, Jack set Jolli to oversee repairs on the sabotaged starfighters. The problem of the sonic jammer soon resolved itself, as Solo and his friends managed to disable the device&mdash;although Jack's chief engineer attempted to convince him to leave Drexel behind with the jammer deactivated, Jack was dead set on confronting Solo. In the meantime, Jolli had managed to restore three of the gang's starfighters, and Jack assigned her to lead the three-person [[Raider Squadron]] to chase the ''Millennium Falcon'' off Drexel's surface. Although Jolli managed to draw the ''Falcon'' into a [[Starfighter combat/Legends|dogfight]], Raider Squadron was unable to ferry the ship into the cruiser's tractor beam. Instead, Solo evaded pursuit with a sudden sharp turn, opening the opportunity for him to destroy two of his pursuers and severely damage Jolli's Y-wing.<ref name="marvel15" />

Still outgunned, Solo had one last trick up his sleeve: he still had a link maintained with Jack's battlecruiser's computer systems, allowing him to wipe every star chart in the ship's navicomputer and essentially trap the gang in the Drexel system. His hand forced, Jack agreed to parley with Solo, ostensibly to work out an exchange of Solo's Rebel treasure for the return of his star charts. As Jack prepared to meet with Solo, he received a plaintive message from Jolli, whose damaged Y-wing was beginning to break apart. Jack immediately denied Jolli's request for a magnetic pulse beam to bring her back to the ship, fearing that it would interfere with his signal system&mdash;he then swiftly forgot about his right-hand woman as she faced death in the void. Jack then donned a [[Breath mask/Legends|breath mask]] and met Solo out in space, protected by the cruiser's magnetic field. Both were armed however, and neither truly intended to parley.<ref name="marvel15" />

Jack had brought plenty of backup, and it appeared that Solo was heavily outgunned, until a badly damaged Y-wing screamed into view. Furious at Jack's abandonment of her, Jolli drove her dying starfighter in a death run towards the cruiser, using the craft's guns to take out Jack's backup. She then pushed her Y-wing into the cruiser's munitions deck, causing a massive explosion that utterly destroyed the ship. Solo shot and killed Crimson Jack in the chaos, conclusively bringing an end to him and his gang.<ref name="marvel15" /> Some time afterward, beings in the employ of Jabba Desilijic Tiure happened across the wreckage of Jack's cruiser, finding that the ship's log remained intact. The log conclusively showed that Han Solo was at fault for the ruin of Jack's gang&mdash;as bankrolling the repairs to Jack's cruiser represented a major investment for the Hutt, Jabba was furious, and placed a sizeable [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] on Solo's head.<ref name="marvel37" />

==Members==
===Crimson Jack===
{{Quote|He thinks, he drinks, he philosophizes! Even if he was a little quick on the trigger himself.|[[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] describes Crimson Jack|<ref name="marvel11" />}}
[[File:CrimsonJackFace.jpg|thumb|right|125px|Crimson Jack]]
The charismatic leader of the gang, Crimson Jack was known for his distinctive red beard and his ruthless ambition. Wanting to use the gang's exploits to become more than just a pirate, Jack transformed the outfit from a common group of raiders on the Outer Rim to something akin to a full-fledged corporation, brokering deals with private investors to help bankroll the gang's activities in exchange for portions of the group's profits.<ref name="marvel12" /> Jack combined a cunning mind with a disregard for the welfare of his underlings, including his close companion Jolli. Jack had long held a grudge against Han Solo, believing the Corellian to be as clever as himself. However, against his better judgment, Jack decided to trust Solo in trying to rob the supposed Rebel treasury on Drexel, which proved to be a fatal mistake. Although Jack managed to get the drop on Solo in their showdown, his lack of care for his subordinates led Jolli&mdash;whom he had abandoned to die in the void&mdash;to make a [[Death/Legends|suicide]] run on Jack's cruiser, leading to his death and the destruction of his gang.<ref name="marvel15" />

===Jolli===
{{Quote|Ah, Jolli! When will you learn that a man can always be killed later... but a lost opportunity is very difficult to revive.|Crimson Jack to Jolli|<ref name="marvel11" />}}
[[File:Jolli.jpg|thumb|left|125px|Jolli]]
The daughter of a fugitive from the Empire, Jolli was orphaned and abandoned as a young girl and left to fend for herself on the galactic frontier. Jolli became skilled with a blaster and a capable starfighter pilot,<ref name="marvel15" /> before joining Jack's gang not long before their fateful trip to the Drexel system.<ref name="marvel7" /> Impressed by her skills and her roiling temper, Jack quickly made Jolli one of his most trusted guns. However, after encountering Han Solo, Jolli developed an unwelcome attraction to the Corellian, which caused her to display violent and erratic behavior as she failed to reconcile her feelings for Solo with a deep hatred of men that stemmed from her father's abandonment.<ref name="marvel13" /> Driven by her compulsion to prove herself as better than any man, Jolli led the gang's starfighter group against the ''Millennium Falcon'', but suffered catastrophic damage to her Y-wing. Infuriated by Jack leaving her to die, Jolli reacted in one final explosion of anger, making a suicide run on the cruiser that led to the gang's utter destruction.<ref name="marvel15" />

==Behind the scenes==
Crimson Jack's pirate gang first appeared in [[Star Wars (1977) 7|''Star Wars'' (1977) 7]], written by [[Roy Thomas]] and released in [[1977]].<ref name="marvel7" /> The gang reappeared in [[Star Wars (1977) 11|''Star Wars'' (1977) 11]],<ref name="marvel11" /> and featured heavily in the next several issues until the group was destroyed in [[Star Wars (1977) 15|''Star Wars'' (1977) 15]].<ref name="marvel15" /> During its appearances in the [[Star Wars (1977)|Marvel ''Star Wars'']] series, the gang was illustrated by [[Howard Chaykin]]<ref name="marvel7" /> and [[Carmine Infantino]].<ref name="marvel11" />
